You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | US Restores Oil Sanctions on Iran and Begins Military Strikes, Driving Sharp Single-Day Rise in Oil Prices; Fed June Meeting Minutes Set to Drop Heavily, Warsh’s Policy Path Draws High Attention (July 8, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News
Fed Dynamics The Fed’s June meeting minutes are set to drop tonight with major market impact. New Chair Kevin Warsh’s policy path is drawing intense attention.
The June FOMC meeting kept the federal funds rate unchanged at 3.50%–3.75%. The statement leaned hawkish, emphasizing economic resilience, inflation still above the 2% target, and the possible removal of the accommodative bias.
New Chair Kevin Warsh’s first complete meeting minutes since taking office will be released at 2:00 AM on July 9 (UTC+8). Markets will closely parse his latest views on inflation, employment, and the long-term policy framework.
The market had previously priced in roughly a 29% chance of a July rate hike, but focus has now shifted to the year-end path. Institutions generally expect the minutes to reinforce a “data-dependent” stance.
Market Impact : Short-term US Treasury yields and the dollar are likely to find support. Equity volatility may rise. Further delays in rate-cut expectations will increase pressure on growth stocks, while clear neutral signals could ease some uncertainty.
International Commodities Middle East geopolitical tensions escalate; crude oil surges sharply while gold and silver come under pressure and pull back.
US Central Command actions and Iran–Israel tensions continue to intensify. The risk premium on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has risen, driving a single-day surge in oil prices.
WTI and Brent crude rose approximately 5.8% and 5.9% respectively over 24 hours, reflecting supply-disruption concerns and safe-haven buying.
Spot gold and silver fell in tandem, pressured by a stronger dollar index and higher Treasury yields.
Market Impact : Oil prices are short-term bullish, but expected EIA inventory builds may cap upside. Precious metals face short-term technical pullbacks but retain long-term inflation-hedge and safe-haven attributes. Institutions advise monitoring how geopolitical developments transmit into energy inflation.
Macroeconomic Policy Services PMI steady but slightly lower; inflation and policy path become the dominant July market theme.
June ISM Services PMI came in at 54.0, slightly below the prior reading but still in expansion territory, underscoring US economic resilience.
Market attention has fully shifted to tonight’s Fed June meeting minutes and upcoming inflation data. Warsh’s new framework-review task force is also in focus.
Geopolitical conflicts are pushing oil prices higher, which could create upward pressure on core inflation via the energy channel and complicate policy decisions.
Market Impact : Policy uncertainty is dominating short-term pricing and amplifying risk-asset volatility. Hawkish signals in the minutes could further strengthen the dollar and Treasuries, putting greater pressure on high-valuation equity sectors.
II. Market Review
Commodities & Forex Performance (Real-time Update)
Spot Gold: ≈ $4,110/oz, +0.08% (24h)
Spot Silver: ≈ $60.039/oz, +0.11% (24h)
WTI Crude: ≈ $71.94/bbl, +2.13% (24h)
Brent Crude: ≈ $75.66/bbl, +2.02% (24h)
US Dollar Index (DXY): ≈ 101.14, +0.05% (24h)
Driving Factors Analysis : Middle East geopolitical tensions (US–Iran actions and Iran–Israel conflict) remain the dominant market variable, directly lifting crude-oil risk premiums and safe-haven demand while reinforcing dollar and Treasury-yield support through energy-inflation expectations, thereby pressuring both gold and silver. The dollar index rose to around 101.17 as capital rotated back into US Treasuries amid uncertainty. Institutional consensus: oil prices are prone to short-term overshoots driven by geopolitics, but global inventory builds and softer demand will limit medium-to-long-term gains. Precious metals face a “strong dollar + high yields” double headwind and are technically weak in the near term; however, any de-escalation or dovish Fed signals could trigger a quick rebound. The linkage is clear: higher oil → inflation concerns → delayed rate-cut expectations → stronger DXY → pressure on gold/silver. Risk appetite and safe-haven demand coexist in the short term, with volatility expected to remain elevated.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC: ≈ $63,595, +0.72%
ETH: ≈ $1,780, +0.97%
Total Crypto Market Cap: ≈ $2.26 trillion, +1%

Below, $62,300–$63,200 holds concentrated long liquidations; a break lower risks cascading long liquidations and added downside pressure.

Performance Summary & Driving Analysis : Tech giants broadly followed the Nasdaq lower, with clear sector differentiation. Semiconductor and AI-related names (MU, AMD, etc.) led declines on concerns over hyperscaler AI capex sustainability and progress in China’s domestic AI chips (DeepSeek etc.). NVDA held up relatively well with a small gain. Traditional mega-caps (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL) eased modestly, reflecting broad pressure on growth stocks in a high-yield, policy-uncertain environment. TSLA’s larger drop may relate to company-specific factors and reduced risk appetite. The biotech M&A highlight (Vertex’s acquisition of CRNX) provided sentiment support for the sector but was insufficient to reverse large-cap tech weakness overall. Institutions note that the AI theme faces short-term valuation digestion and requires more real-world adoption data and earnings delivery. With geopolitics and Fed minutes as dual variables, markets remain cautious in the near term; focus on high-quality names with strong fundamentals and stable cash flow for differentiation opportunities.

NVDA’s modest resilience was not enough to stem the broader sector weakness.

Market Interpretation : Although Nvidia posted a modest gain, the sector’s broad weakness reflects cautious revaluation of the AI theme in a high-valuation environment. Institutions believe AMD retains competitiveness in data-center and AI-accelerator cards but needs more order and gross-margin data in the near term to confirm growth sustainability. China’s DeepSeek and similar developments are viewed as longer-term competitive signals rather than immediate threats.
[...]
Investment Implications : AMD is best followed alongside Q2 earnings and AI-product updates. Consider pairing with leaders such as NVDA in a diversified portfolio to manage single-sector exposure.
